question: Which HTML tag is used to create a bulleted list where the order of items does not matter? 📝
explanation: Brilliant! The <ul> tag stands for Unordered List, which creates a bulleted list for items where the sequence isn't important. 🚀

question: If you want to display a step-by-step recipe, which tag is best suited to create an ordered numbered list? 🍳
explanation: Spot on! The <ol> tag stands for Ordered List, which automatically numbers your list items sequentially. 👨‍🍳

question: Which tag is placed inside a <ul> or <ol> tag to define each individual item in the list? 🛒
explanation: Awesome! The <li> tag stands for List Item and is required to add elements inside both ordered and unordered lists. ✨

question: What is the default bullet style for an unordered list (<ul>) in a web browser? 🎨
explanation: Great job! Browsers use a solid round black dot called a 'disc' as the default bullet for unordered lists. 💻

question: Which attribute can you add to the <ol> tag to change the numbering style to uppercase Roman numerals? 🏛️
explanation: Perfect! The type attribute defines the numbering style, and type="I" sets it to uppercase Roman numerals like I, II, III. ⭐
hint: You need to specify the 'type' of numbering.

question: How can you make an ordered list start counting from the number 5 instead of 1? 🏁
explanation: Fantastic! The start attribute tells the browser exactly which number to begin the ordered list from. 🎉
hint: Think about where you 'start' a race.

question: Which set of tags is used to create a Description List, usually used for a glossary or dictionary of terms? 📖
explanation: Excellent! A Description List uses <dl> for the list, <dt> for the term, and <dd> for the definition. 🎓
hint: Look for the tags starting with the letter 'd'.

question: Which HTML tag is used to embed an image onto a webpage? 🖼️
explanation: Superb! The tag is an empty tag used to display images on a webpage. 🌟
hint: It is a three-letter abbreviation for 'image'.

question: Which attribute of the tag specifies the path to the image file? 📍
explanation: Bingo! The src (source) attribute tells the browser where to find the image file to load it. 🔍

question: Why is the 'alt' attribute crucial when using the tag? ♿
options: It adds a border to the image 🖼️
It provides alternative text if the image fails to load 📝
It makes the image download faster ⚡
answer: It provides alternative text if the image fails to load 📝
explanation: Brilliant! The alt attribute makes your site accessible by describing the image for screen readers and displaying text if the image link breaks. 🙌

question: If you want an image to be exactly 200 pixels wide, which attribute should you use inside the tag? 📏
explanation: Spot on! The width attribute directly sets how wide the image should appear on the webpage. 🖥️

question: Does the tag require a closing tag like ? 🧩
options: No, it is an empty tag 🔴
Only if it has a caption 🟡
answer: No, it is an empty tag 🔴
explanation: Awesome! The tag only contains attributes and does not wrap any text, so it is an empty tag with no closing tag. 🛡️
hint: Think about whether it holds any text content inside it.

question: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink that connects one webpage to another? 🔗
explanation: Fantastic! The <a> (anchor) tag is the fundamental building block for creating links between webpages. 🗺️

question: Which attribute in the <a> tag holds the destination URL of the hyperlink? 🎯
explanation: Great job! The href (hypertext reference) attribute specifies the exact web address the link should navigate to. 🚀

question: How do you make a hyperlink open in a brand new browser tab or window? 🪟
explanation: Perfect! Adding target="_blank" tells the browser to safely open the linked page in a completely new tab. 💻
hint: You want the target to be a 'blank' new page.

question: What is the default text color of an unvisited hyperlink in most web browsers? 🖌️
explanation: Spot on! By default, browsers underline hyperlinks and color them blue before they have been clicked. 🎨
hint: It's the color of the sky.

question: How can you create an email link that automatically opens the user's email client? ✉️
explanation: Superb! Using 'mailto:' inside the href attribute triggers the device's default email program to compose a new message. 💌
hint: You want to 'mail to' a specific address.

question: Which tag is used to define a table in HTML? 📊
explanation: Awesome! The <table> tag acts as the main container for all the rows and cells of your data grid. 🧩
hint: The name of the tag is the same as the structure itself.

question: Inside a table, which tag is used to create a single horizontal row? 🛤️
explanation: Brilliant! The <tr> tag stands for Table Row and contains the data cells for that specific horizontal line. 📏

question: Which tag is used to create a standard data cell inside a table row? 🧊
explanation: Excellent! The <td> tag stands for Table Data, representing a single cell containing text, images, or other elements. 💎

question: To create a table header cell that is bold and centered by default, which tag should you use? 🎩
explanation: Great job! The <th> tag stands for Table Heading and automatically styles the text as bold and centered to stand out. ✨

question: Which table attribute is used to define the thickness of the line drawn around the table and its cells? 🖼️
explanation: Fantastic! The border attribute specifies the width of the grid lines surrounding the table cells in pixels. 🖋️
hint: It's the boundary around a picture or table.

question: If you want a single table cell to span vertically across three rows, which attribute do you use? ↕️
explanation: Spot on! The rowspan attribute tells the cell to stretch downward, covering multiple rows like a giant block. 🏗️

question: To merge a cell horizontally across multiple columns, which attribute is applied to the <td> or <th> tag? ↔️
explanation: Perfect! The colspan attribute stretches a single cell left-to-right across the specified number of columns. 🌉

question: Which tag is used to add a descriptive title or heading directly above a table? 📝
explanation: Awesome! The <caption> tag provides a clear title for the table, usually appearing perfectly centered at the top. 👑
hint: It's the same word used for text describing a picture.

question: Which table attribute controls the empty space between the cell border and the content inside the cell? 🎈
explanation: Brilliant! Cellpadding acts like a cushion inside the cell, keeping text from touching the borders. 🛋️
hint: Think of adding 'padding' to the inside.

question: Which table attribute defines the space between completely separate adjacent cells? 🌌
explanation: Superb! Cellspacing controls the gap or distance strictly between the outer walls of individual table cells. 🧱

question: Which HTML element acts as a container to collect user inputs like text, passwords, and selections? 📝
explanation: Great job! The <form> tag wraps all input fields, buttons, and checkboxes so the data can be submitted together. 📦
hint: You fill this out at a doctor's office or online.

question: Which versatile tag is most commonly used inside a form to accept different kinds of typed data from a user? ⌨️
explanation: Fantastic! The <input> tag is highly flexible and changes its behavior based on its 'type' attribute. 🛠️

question: To create a single-line text box for someone's first name, which input type is used? 👤
explanation: Spot on! Using <input type="text"> creates a standard box where users can type visible alphanumeric characters. 🖋️

question: Which input type masks the user's typing with dots or asterisks for security? 🔒
explanation: Perfect! The password type safely hides the characters as they are typed to prevent shoulder-surfing. 🛡️
hint: It is used to protect your accounts.

question: If you want a user to select ONLY ONE option from a list (like selecting gender), which input type is best? 🔘
explanation: Awesome! Radio buttons allow only one selection from a grouped set, just like the old station buttons on a car radio. 🚗
hint: Think of an old audio device.

question: How do you ensure multiple radio buttons belong to the exact same group so only one can be picked? 🔗
explanation: Brilliant! Giving radio buttons the identical 'name' attribute binds them together as a mutually exclusive group. 🤝
hint: They must share the same 'name' family.

question: Which input type allows users to select MULTIPLE options from a list (like choosing hobbies)? ✅
explanation: Excellent! Checkboxes act independently, meaning users can check zero, one, or several boxes in a form. 🎯

question: Which tag creates a dropdown list menu for users to choose an option from? 🔽
explanation: Great job! The <select> tag creates the dropdown menu container, and <option> tags define the choices inside it. 📌

question: Which tag is placed inside a <select> dropdown list to define the individual clickable choices? 🖱️
explanation: Fantastic! Every <option> tag inside a <select> element represents one item in the dropdown menu. 📂
hint: You are giving the user an 'option'.

question: If you want a user to type a long paragraph or message, which form tag should you use? 📝
explanation: Superb! The <textarea> element creates a multi-line input box, perfect for comments, essays, or feedback. 💬

question: Which input type generates a button that securely sends the gathered form data to a server? 🚀
explanation: Spot on! The submit button gathers all the inputs and triggers the form to send its data to the backend processor. 🌐

question: Which attribute of the <form> tag specifies the URL of the file that will process the submitted data? 📍
explanation: Awesome! The action attribute tells the browser exactly where to send the form data when the submit button is clicked. 🎯

question: Which attribute of the <form> tag defines HOW the data is sent, usually as 'GET' or 'POST'? 📬
explanation: Perfect! The method attribute specifies the HTTP method (GET or POST) used to transmit the form data securely. 🔐

question: What happens when you click an <input type="reset"> button inside a form? 🔄
options: It clears all fields to their default values 🧹
answer: It clears all fields to their default values 🧹
explanation: Brilliant! The reset button is a quick way to wipe the slate clean and clear all user inputs in the form at once. ✨

question: Which attribute is used inside an <input> tag to uniquely identify it for CSS and JavaScript? 🆔
explanation: Excellent! The 'id' attribute must be absolutely unique on the page, making it perfect for linking labels or scripts to that specific input. 🎯

question: What is the purpose of the 'value' attribute in an <input type="text"> field? 🖋️
options: It pre-fills the text box with default text 📝
answer: It pre-fills the text box with default text 📝
explanation: Great job! The 'value' attribute defines the initial data inside the input box before the user even types anything. ✏️
hint: It defines the starting 'value' of the field.

question: Can you put an image tag inside an anchor tag ? 🖼️🔗
options: Yes, it creates a clickable image 🖱️
Only if the image is a PNG 🖼️
answer: Yes, it creates a clickable image 🖱️
explanation: Fantastic! Wrapping an image inside an anchor tag turns the entire image into a button or clickable link. 🚀
hint: Think about website logos that you can click to go home.

question: How do you create a hyperlink that navigates directly to an element with id="top" on the same webpage? ⬇️
explanation: Superb! Using the hashtag (#) followed by the element's id creates an anchor link that scrolls you directly to that section. 🎢
hint: It requires the symbol often called a hashtag or pound sign.

question: Which combination of attributes allows a table data cell to cover an area of 2 rows and 2 columns simultaneously? 🔲
explanation: Spot on! You can safely combine both rowspan and colspan in a single <td> to make large, grid-spanning cells. 🏗️
hint: You need to stretch both 'rows' and 'columns'.

question: Which table attribute can be added directly to the <table> tag to align the entire table to the center of the page? ⚖️
explanation: Perfect! While often done in CSS today, the classic align="center" attribute directly centers the table element on the webpage. 🌟

question: What does a browser typically do if the image specified in the 'src' attribute cannot be found? ❓
options: It shows a broken image icon and the 'alt' text 🖼️
It skips loading the rest of the page 🛑
answer: It shows a broken image icon and the 'alt' text 🖼️
explanation: Awesome! When a link breaks, the browser gracefully degrades by showing a small broken icon and displaying your helpful 'alt' text. 🛠️
hint: This is why the 'alt' attribute is so important!

question: In an HTML form, what is the role of the <label> tag? 🏷️
options: It links descriptive text to a specific input field 🔗
It creates a new submit button 🚀
answer: It links descriptive text to a specific input field 🔗
explanation: Brilliant! The <label> tag improves usability; clicking the label text automatically focuses on or selects its connected input field. 🎯
hint: It puts a 'label' on the input so you know what it is.

question: Which attribute of the tag defines text that briefly appears when a user hovers their mouse pointer over the image? 🖱️
explanation: Excellent! The 'title' attribute produces a small tooltip popup containing extra information when the mouse hovers over the element. ✨
